                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of a thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain, acyclovir and famciclovir are ineffective as they require thymidine kinase for activation. Ganciclovir, however, is activated by a different kinase, making it effective against thymidine kinase-deficient strains. Cidofovir does not require any viral kinase for activation, thus it remains effective against such strains. Amantadine is not suitable as it targets influenza viruses, not varicella-zoster. Therefore, the best antiviral agents for this population would be ganciclovir and cidofovir, with ganciclovir having a slightly higher preference due to its specific activation pathway.
